title: The desktop update host serves Windows and Linux feeds, signatures and installers, records each install's platform and each browser download per OS, while a Mac app gets the same answers as before
steps: S1: With TEST_DATABASE_URL set to a Postgres the tests may create schemas in, run node --test apps/tracy-web/test/desktop-update.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/desktop-download.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/desktop-install-platform.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/ops-app-statistic.test.mjs.
expect: S1: stable.yml (win), dev-linux.yml and dev-linux-arm64.yml (linux) stream with no-store and record the install with platform win / linux and the x-arch header.
S1: <channel file>.sig for the four channel-file names streams with no-store as application/octet-stream and records nothing.
S1: .exe, .AppImage and .deb, flat or under <channel>/<version>/<build id>/, stream with their IANA content types and no-store; a GET writes no desktop_install row.

S1: .blockmap, latest.yml, latest-mac.yml, stable-win.yml, stable-linux-armv7l.yml, a .sig of anything but a channel file, a channel file or manifest.json inside a release folder, .msi, .rpm and lowercase .appimage answer 404 without asking the store.
S1: stable-mac.yml, flat and foldered zip and dmg answer the same status, body and headers as before; the mac read records platform mac; the two dmg GETs record two downloads.

S1: migration 086 files a desktop_install row written before it as mac and refuses a platform outside mac/win/linux; /ops/desktop/installs has an OS column (macOS / Windows / Linux + version) and no macOS column; App Statistic installs report macos / windows / linux.

S1: a browser GET of Tracy-Cowork-<v>-win-<arch>-setup.exe, -linux-<arch>.AppImage or .deb writes a desktop_download row with platform windows/linux, arch, channel, version and utm source; the same GET carrying App-Name or App-Version (the app's updater) writes nothing and sets no cookie; dmg metadata is unchanged.
S1: App Statistic filters downloads, installs and users by platform=macos|windows|linux, lists the platforms in options, and refuses any other value.
fence: The update host refuses every name outside the per-platform contract before the store is asked; only a channel-file read records an install; an updater fetch of an installer is never a download

tests: the Windows channel file is streamed
each channel file has a detached signature
names outside the contract are refused
086 files every install recorded before it as mac
an install reports the platform whose channel file it read
Windows and Linux installer names give platform
a browser GET of an exe, AppImage or deb counts
Windows and Linux downloads are stored with platform
downloads and installs filter by operating system
